model_note: CRP.NZ is NOT a growth-DCF or owner-FCF candidate, routed per the dcf-methods SKILL.md 'Distressed, receivership, delisted, cash shell' row to an asset/scenario waterfall. The company has recorded zero revenue in its entire disclosed history (FY2016-9M FY2026), carries a recurring going-concern qualification (current liabilities exceeded current assets by CAD$364,985 at 31-Dec-2025, cash of only CAD$71,441), was delisted from the TSX-V effective 31-Jul-2026, and has had its NZX trading SUSPENDED since 3-Aug-2026 pending a direct-listing application. There is no owner free cash flow to project: the business has never produced revenue and cannot commence mining on either of its two flagship assets (Chatham Rise seabed phosphate, Makatea land phosphate) without regulatory consents that have already been refused once (Chatham Rise Marine Consent, declined Feb-2015) and remain ungranted after more than a decade. The entire balance sheet (CAD$6.81m total assets) is almost wholly intangible mineral property interests (Chatham Rise $4.69m, Makatea $1.94m, Korella $0.18m) whose realizable value is contingent, binary, and unrelated to any cash-flow stream. This model instead scenario-weights the realizable claim on those mineral interests, net of (a) the heavy discount the market and any acquirer would apply to an unpermitted asset with a decade-long refusal history, and (b) the dilution of CRP shareholders' economic interest in the flagship Chatham Rise subsidiary caused by the Wetstone Global earn-in structure, which can convert into up to 75% of that subsidiary.

inputs.net_debt_note: No bank debt; only trade/other payables (CAD$525,375 total, of which CAD$222,194 is related-party payables to directors) and a nil lease-liability balance at 31-Dec-2025 (fully repaid; was CAD$29,412 at FY2025). 'Net debt' here is reported as negative cash (net cash) for schema completeness only -- it is NOT subtracted from a discounted cash flow, because no cash-flow stream is being discounted. All liabilities are already netted off inside the segment/consolidated equity figures used directly in the scenario waterfall below.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Nine months ended 31-Dec-2025 combined operating and investing cash outflow of CAD$412,334 (9M FY2026), per CRP.NZ_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt:279. Shown for schema completeness / disclosure only -- not used as a DCF base, because the company is pre-revenue and this outflow is structurally funded by dilutive equity raises and related-party support, not a return-generating operating flow.
inputs.sbc_source: CRP.NZ_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt:1626-1632 -- 8,750,000 fully-vested director options granted 24-Nov-2025, exercise price CAD$0.054, Black-Scholes expense CAD$331,225 (FY2026 to date). Shown for disclosure; not used to adjust a cash-flow DCF, which this model does not build.
inputs.share_growth_note: Share count has grown continuously via dilutive private placements every year on record: 15.5m (FY2018) -> 20.1m (FY2019) -> 25.7m (FY2020) -> 34.6m (FY2021) -> 63.3m (FY2022) -> 85.0m (FY2023) -> 90.0m (FY2024) -> 103.3m (FY2025) -> 115.4m (9M FY2026), i.e. roughly 7.5x over 8 years. This dilution is treated qualitatively via the scenario narratives (continued placements are the base-case funding mechanism) rather than as a projected compounding share-count path, because there is no cash-flow-per-share base being compounded.
inputs.fx_note: CAD/NZD = 1.2453 (1 CAD buys 1.2453 NZD) per Yahoo Finance CADNZD=X, retrieved 2026-09-25. All filings, the segment note, and the balance-sheet figures below are in CAD as reported. The NZX quote is in NZD. Every CAD scenario value is converted to NZD at this spot rate for direct comparison with current_price. No dual listing remains to parity-check against (TSX-V delisted 31-Jul-2026), so this is a spot FX conversion only, not a cross-checked parity rate.
inputs.units: CAD dollars (whole/absolute, not thousands or millions) for all monetary figures except shares_outstanding, which is in millions per the standard schema convention
inputs.price_as_of_note: CRITICAL: this is a FROZEN quote, not a live price. NZX trading in CRP.NZ has been suspended since 3-Aug-2026 (per Analysis.json recent_developments and the TSX-V delisting that removed CRP's foreign-exempt-issuer status). Yahoo's regularMarketTime of 2026-07-31 predates the suspension by only 3 days -- i.e. this was very close to the LAST trade before suspension took effect, not a stale quote from months earlier. However, daily closes from Yahoo's chart series show an IDENTICAL 0.038 print forward-filled every trading day from early September through 24-Sep-2026 (the query date), which is the classic frozen-last-trade artifact for a suspended/delisted ticker (per MEMORY.md's stale-price-delisted-tickers.md pattern: regularMarketTime + flat/null tail bars). The price is flagged VOLATILE/STALE for this reason: it reflects the last executable trade before a trading halt whose resolution (a direct NZX listing application) is still pending, not current market-clearing information, and should be replaced at the next confirmed live trade once (if) trading resumes.
inputs.balance_sheet_source: CRP.NZ_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt (nine months ended 31-Dec-2025, the most recent filing extracted; NZ/Canada fiscal year end 31-March)
inputs.wacc_rationale: not_applicable -- no discounted cash-flow stream is built; see valuation_philosophy
inputs.lease_treatment: Lease liability fully repaid to nil at 31-Dec-2025 (was CAD$29,412 at FY2025 year-end); immaterial to the valuation either way
inputs.nci_treatment: No third-party NCI currently exists at the CRP consolidated level. The economically equivalent construct here is the WETSTONE GLOBAL earn-in: a convertible working-capital loan (USD$150,000 initial, Aug-2025, 10% stepping to 12.5%+) that on conversion can claim up to 75% of Chatham Rock Phosphate (NZ) Limited, the subsidiary holding the flagship Chatham Rise asset. This is modelled as a direct haircut to CRP shareholders' retained economic share of the Chatham Rise segment value in each scenario (25% retained in bear, ~60% in base, 70% in bull), rather than as a classic NCI line, because the conversion has not yet occurred and its ultimate percentage is scenario-dependent (subject to due diligence completion and the definitive investment agreement terms).
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE: asset/scenario waterfall per .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md routing table row 'Distressed, receivership, delisted, cash shell -> Asset or creditor waterfall -- not a going-concern model'. Chosen over owner-FCF DCF because: (1) zero revenue in 9+ years of disclosed history with no path to revenue absent a regulatory consent already refused once; (2) recurring going-concern qualification with negative working capital every recent period; (3) TSX-V delisting (Jul-2026) and NZX trading suspension (Aug-2026) mean there is currently no live, tradeable market price at all; (4) the dominant balance-sheet item (CAD$6.7m mineral property interests) is a binary regulatory-approval claim, not a cash-generating or even a stably-held asset. This follows the same methodology precedent as AFC.NZ (research/AFC.NZ/Reports/AFC.NZ_DCF.json), adapted for CRP's materially different fact pattern: CRP is not audit-disclaimed and has a genuine (if unpermitted) mineral resource rather than a collapsed operating business, but faces its own distinct dilution risk via the Wetstone earn-in rather than a controlling-shareholder debt-forgiveness dynamic. First valuation of this ticker (no prior DCF/Drivers.json existed).

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue and EPS CAGRs are null/not meaningful: CRP has recorded revenue of exactly CAD$0 or an immaterial ~CAD$5,000/year (likely incidental/non-operating) in every fiscal year FY2016-9M FY2026, and EPS has been negative in every period, precluding a meaningful compound growth rate. Equity CAGR is modestly positive over 5 years (+8.7%) but this reflects periodic capital injections via share placements diluting into book value, not organic earnings growth or value creation -- shareholders' equity has been essentially flat to declining in real terms (CAD$4.3-7.3m range across 9 years) despite the company raising and spending well over CAD$10m cumulative in that period, because losses have consumed almost all raised capital.
historical_growth.notes: No owner-FCF series exists to CAGR -- FCF has been negative in every disclosed period without exception (FY2016 through 9M FY2026), driven entirely by pre-revenue exploration/corporate overhead spend, not by SBC or working-capital timing. This is why the model abandons FCF projection entirely.

base.narrative: Shell persists on continued life support. No Marine Consent re-application resolution and no Makatea Mining Concession grant occur within the valuation horizon. The Group continues to fund itself through repeated dilutive private placements (as in every year FY2018-FY2026, most recently CAD$0.05/share raises in Jul-2025 and Dec-2025) and director forbearance on related-party payables. The Wetstone Global due-diligence process (nine-month exclusivity from 4-Jul-2025, i.e. through approximately Apr-2026) progresses and the definitive investment agreement is executed on terms partway toward the maximum 75% conversion cap, leaving CRP with an estimated ~60% retained economic interest in the Chatham Rise NZ subsidiary. Mineral property carrying values are held at a substantial (50%) haircut to book, reflecting the unresolved decade-long permit overhang, without assuming outright impairment to zero.
base.discounting_note: No perpetuity cash-flow stream exists to discount -- the company is pre-revenue with no forecast path to production absent an unresolved regulatory consent. Value is built as a haircut-book asset claim, not a discounted flow.

bull.narrative: Either the Chatham Rise Marine Consent re-application succeeds, or the Makatea Mining Concession is granted by French Polynesia's Council of Ministers (both are live, disclosed processes, though timing and outcome are explicitly uncertain in the FY2026 filings). A grant materially improves CRP's negotiating position with Wetstone, reducing execution urgency and the ultimate conversion percentage (~30% assumed, i.e. CRP retains ~70% of Chatham Rise). Mineral assets re-rate above book value (Chatham Rise to 1.5x book, Makatea to 1.2x book) reflecting the embedded optionality of a now-permitted, 20-year-tenure mining project, but well short of a full construction-stage NPV, since substantial development capital, construction execution risk, and offtake/pricing risk remain unresolved even after a consent is granted.

bear.narrative: The Chatham Rise Marine Consent re-application fails a second time (consistent with the EPA's 2015 finding of significant and permanent adverse effects and the further 2023/2024 change-of-conditions refusal), and/or the Wetstone relationship or an equivalent financing source is withdrawn, forcing the Group into a distressed wind-down. Wetstone converts its loan into the maximum 75% of the Chatham Rise NZ subsidiary (or an equivalent dilutive rescue financing occurs), leaving CRP with a residual 25% economic interest in a now heavily impaired (90% haircut) Chatham Rise asset. Makatea similarly fails to secure its Mining Concession. Cash and any free liquidity is consumed by wind-down costs and existing payables (including CAD$222,194 owed to related-party directors) ahead of any residual to ordinary equity.

base.note: No revenue or FCF is projected -- the company has zero disclosed revenue history and its entire near-term future is contingent on binary regulatory outcomes, not organic growth. Value is a static asset-haircut claim, not a projected flow.

bull.note: Even in the bull case, no production revenue is modelled within this horizon -- a Marine Consent or Mining Concession grant is a necessary precondition to construction, which would itself take years to complete. Bull value is captured entirely as the re-rated optionality value of the underlying mineral asset, not as a cash-flow projection.

bear.note: Wind-down/dilution-to-25%-retained-interest scenario; no revenue in any case.

base.methodology: intrinsic_value_cad = (Chatham Rise book CAD$4,690,436 x 50% haircut x 60% CRP-retained share) + (Makatea book CAD$1,937,487 x 50% haircut) + (Korella book CAD$180,940 x 50% haircut) + cash CAD$71,441, all / 115,410,765 shares = CAD$0.021989/share. Converted to NZD at 1.2453 = NZD$0.027383/share (this is the quote-currency 'intrinsic_value' field).

bull.methodology: intrinsic_value_cad = (Chatham Rise book x 1.5x re-rate x 70% CRP-retained) + (Makatea book x 1.2x) + (Korella book x 1.0x) + cash, all / shares = CAD$0.065005/share -> NZD$0.080951/share at 1.2453.

bear.methodology: intrinsic_value_cad = (Chatham Rise book x 10% residual value x 25% CRP-retained after Wetstone max 75% conversion) + (Makatea book x 10% residual) + (Korella book x 25% residual) + CAD$0 residual cash to equity after wind-down costs and payables, all / shares = CAD$0.003087/share -> NZD$0.003844/share at 1.2453.

entry_price.not_meaningful_note: A standard 15%-IRR entry-price formula assumes a cash-generating (or at minimum, cash-distributing) asset whose future flows can be discounted back to a purchase price today. CRP generates no revenue, pays no dividends, and every scenario's 'exit value' is either a static, haircut asset claim (base, bear) or a binary re-rate on an uncertain regulatory grant (bull) -- there is no modelled cash-flow stream to which an IRR hurdle can be applied. Per the AFC.NZ precedent for this model family, entry price is instead reported as the probability-weighted intrinsic value itself: the price at which a buyer pays fair value across the three scenarios, with no presumption of a return path beyond the scenario re-rating itself.

recommended_entry_price.note: For this non-cash-flowing, pre-revenue shell, the decision-useful 'entry price' is the probability-weighted fair value across the three scenarios (see probability_weighted.weighted_iv) -- NZD$0.026003/share, versus the last (frozen, suspended) quoted price of NZD$0.038/share.

sensitivity.description: A standard WACC / terminal-growth grid is not meaningful here (no cash-flow stream to discount). Instead this matrix sensitizes the base-case intrinsic value (NZD/share) to (rows) the haircut applied to the Chatham Rise mineral asset book value, and (columns) CRP's retained economic percentage of that asset after the Wetstone earn-in converts.
sensitivity.matrix_read_note: Row = Chatham Rise book-value haircut (10% = only a mild discount to the disclosed CAD$4.69m carrying value; 90% = near write-off, consistent with a second consent refusal). Column = CRP's retained economic share of Chatham Rise after the Wetstone earn-in (25% = Wetstone converts to its maximum 75% stake; 85% = Wetstone's option is never exercised or lapses). Makatea and Korella held at the base-case 50% haircut and cash at CAD$71,441 in every cell for consistency. Every cell assumes Wetstone's conversion percentage is fixed at the column value for illustration; in practice the earn-in terms and the permit outcome are correlated (a consent grant plausibly both reduces the haircut AND reduces Wetstone's eventual stake, which is what the bull scenario models jointly rather than holding one variable fixed).

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear is weighted just below base (40% vs 45%) rather than dominant, reflecting: (1) the Chatham Rise Marine Consent has already been refused once (2015) AND a related change-of-conditions application was refused again in 2023/2024 -- a real, demonstrated pattern of regulatory failure, not a hypothetical risk; (2) the Wetstone earn-in's maximum 75% conversion cap was itself INCREASED from 70% to 75% in Jul-2026, suggesting the terms are moving against existing CRP shareholders as the company's negotiating position weakens with each additional dilutive raise; (3) recurring going-concern qualification with negative working capital (CAD$364,985 deficit at 9M FY2026) and cash of only CAD$71,441; (4) the TSX-V delisting and NZX trading suspension materially impair the company's ability to raise fresh capital on any terms, let alone favourable ones, at exactly the moment its cash runway is shortest. Base (45%) is nonetheless the modal outcome because CRP has, in fact, successfully raised capital via placement in EVERY year since at least FY2018 without ever actually running out of cash or being wound up, and management continues to characterise the going-concern basis as appropriate with explicit fallback options (farm-down, asset sale) disclosed. Bull (15%, materially lower than a typical base-rate operating company's bull weight) reflects that BOTH the Marine Consent re-application and the Makatea Mining Concession are genuinely live, disclosed regulatory processes (not merely aspirational) -- but a decade-plus of delay and one outright refusal on the flagship asset means a favourable resolution within the modelled horizon is a real possibility, not the central case.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.checks_replaced: model is asset_waterfall: no multiples rule applies; the historical table is reported for context only
sanity_check.fix_applied: asset/scenario waterfall valuation instead of a growth or owner-FCF DCF; current_price flagged as a frozen/suspended quote rather than a live market-clearing price

valuation_philosophy.summary: CRP.NZ is a pre-revenue mineral explorer whose entire value rests on two binary, unresolved regulatory approvals (the Chatham Rise Marine Consent and the Makatea Mining Concession) and is currently further complicated by (a) a dilutive earn-in financing structure that can hand up to 75% of the flagship Chatham Rise subsidiary to a single counterparty (Wetstone Global), and (b) a trading suspension on its sole remaining listing (NZX) following delisting from the TSX-V. No cash-flow-based valuation model applies: the company has never earned revenue, has no path to revenue without a consent already refused once, and funds itself entirely through continuous, highly dilutive equity placements. This asset/scenario waterfall instead haircuts the disclosed mineral-property carrying values (Chatham Rise CAD$4.69m, Makatea CAD$1.94m, Korella CAD$0.18m) for permit-refusal risk and for the CRP shareholders' retained economic share after the Wetstone earn-in, producing a probability-weighted fair value of NZD$0.0260/share against a FROZEN last-traded price of NZD$0.038/share.
key_risks_to_valuation: Marine Consent re-application outcome (single largest value driver; refused once already in 2015, with a further related refusal in 2023/2024)
Wetstone Global earn-in conversion percentage (contractually capped at up to 75% of the Chatham Rise NZ subsidiary, raised from 70% as recently as Jul-2026)
Continued access to dilutive equity capital markets given the TSX-V delisting and NZX trading suspension -- if placements become impossible while suspended, the going-concern basis itself is at risk
Makatea Mining Concession timeline and outcome (French Polynesia Council of Ministers process, repeatedly guided as imminent across multiple prior years without resolution)
Whether/when NZX trading resumes at all following the direct-listing application -- an unresolved process with no disclosed timeline in the filings reviewed
